page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 processors. It features 96 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture running at 3.3 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 5700 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Single-core performance sits in the average tier. Database operations, including Redis SET operations and PassMark database tests, also rank in the top tier. For machine learning workloads, the instance achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds for small LLM models and strong performance for medium-sized models, though text generation speeds for small models fall into the average tier.

The instance provides high resource density by combining 96 dedicated physical cores with a substantial 5700 GB local NVMe SSD storage allocation. This bundled storage eliminates the need for external block storage for high-throughput local operations, improving qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive workloads. However, tradeoffs include the lack of hardware-accelerated GPUs and x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX, which limits its applicability for heavy GPU-accelerated tasks or legacy x86 software.

This hardware profile is suited for high-throughput database deployments, large-scale web serving, multi-threaded data compression tasks, and medium-scale language model inference. The combination of high memory bandwidth, dedicated physical cores, and fast local NVMe storage supports intensive general-purpose and storage-heavy applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.24xlarge is an ARM64-based general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processors. It features 96 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz, 384.0 GB of RAM, and 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it delivers 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and exceptional database and Redis SET operations. While single-core performance and small-model text generation are average, its multi-threaded capabilities and high-speed local storage offer strong qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense workloads. This instance is suited for database hosting, static web serving, multi-threaded data processing, and medium-scale LLM inference.
